keyVerseText: And what shall I more say? for the time would fail me to tell of Gedeon, and of Barak, and of Samson, and of Jephthae; of David also, and Samuel, and of the prophets:
rootMeaning: The name Σαμψών (Sampsṓn) derives from the Hebrew שִׁמְשׁוֹן (Shimshôwn), which literally means "like the sun." This root conveys imagery of brightness, strength, and power, reflecting the character of Samson as a figure endowed with extraordinary might. The etymology enriches the English name by connecting it to the symbolism of the sun, suggesting illumination and divine empowerment beyond a mere personal identifier.
usageInScripture: The term Σαμψών appears only once in the New Testament, specifically in Hebrews 11:32, where it is translated as "Samson." This singular occurrence underscores the consistency of the name's use as a proper noun referring to the Israelite judge known for his Nazirite vow and heroic exploits. The translation "of Samson" in this context highlights his role among other notable figures of faith, emphasizing his inclusion in the biblical narrative of God's deliverance through chosen leaders.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding the original meaning of Σαμψών as "like the sun" deepens our appreciation of Samson's role in Scripture as a divinely empowered judge. His life exemplifies the paradox of human weakness and God's strength working through flawed vessels. From a Christ-centered perspective, Samson's story prefigures the ultimate light and strength found in Christ, who overcomes darkness and judges with perfect justice. Recognizing the Hebrew root reminds believers that God’s purposes shine through individuals despite their imperfections, calling us to trust in His enabling power.
keyVerseReflection: Hebrews 11:32 mentions Samson alongside other heroic figures, stating, "And what shall I more say? for the time would fail me to tell of Gedeon, and of Barak, and of Samson, and of Jephthae; of David also, and Samuel, and of the prophets." The use of Σαμψών here emphasizes Samson's place in the 'hall of faith,' highlighting his significance as a model of faithfulness despite personal struggles. This reference invites believers to reflect on how God’s strength was demonstrated through Samson’s life and encourages faith in God’s power to work through His people.
